arguments.content:
-- Arena 2D director: three balls on Rigidbody 2Ds; the arrow keys push the first one.
---@class Arena : ScriptInstance
local Arena = {
    properties = {
        { name = "duration", displayName = "Duration (frames)", type = "int", default = 180 },
        { name = "push", displayName = "Push (m/s per step)", type = "float", default = 0.12 },
        { name = "cloud", displayName = "Cloud", type = "Sprite" },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Arena:init()
    T.enter("Arena2D")
    T.schedule("Arena2D", { { Input.KEY_RIGHT, 30, 60 }, { Input.KEY_LEFT, 90, 105 } })
    self.balls = {}
    for i = 1, 3 do
        local e = self.scene:findEntity("Ball " .. i)
        if e ~= 0 then self.balls[#self.balls + 1] = Rigidbody2D(self.scene, e) end
    end
    self.hits = 0
    RegisterEvent(self, self.scene:getPhysicsSystem().beginContact2D, "onBeginContact")
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onFixedUpdate")
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onPostUpdate")
    T.log("setup", #self.balls, self.cloud ~= nil)
end

function Arena:onBeginContact(bodyA, shapeA, bodyB, shapeB)
    self.hits = self.hits + 1
end

function Arena:onFixedUpdate()
    local ball = self.balls[1]
    if not ball then return end
    local dir = 0
    if T.held(Input.KEY_RIGHT) then dir = dir + 1 end
    if T.held(Input.KEY_LEFT) then dir = dir - 1 end
    if dir ~= 0 then
        ball:applyLinearImpulseToCenter(Vector2(dir * self.push * ball:getMass(), 0), true)
    end
end

function Arena:onPostUpdate()
    local f = T.frame
    if f % 10 == 0 then
        for i, ball in ipairs(self.balls) do
            T.log("ball", i, ball.position, ball.linearVelocity, ball.angle)
        end
    end
    if f % 30 == 0 and self.cloud then
        T.log("cloud", self.cloud.position)
    end
    if f == self.duration then
        T.log("summary", self.hits > 0)
        T.finish()
    end
    T.step()
end

return Arena

-- The beacon bobs with an Animation Clip on its Animation Player; the clip's event calls
-- onBeaconPulse.
---@class Beacon : ScriptInstance
local Beacon = {
    properties = {
        { name = "clip", displayName = "Clip", type = "string", default = "Hover" },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Beacon:init()
    self.go = GameObject(self.scene, self.entity)
    self.player = self.go:getAnimationPlayer()
    self.pulses = 0
    self.started = -1
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function Beacon:onUpdate()
    if not self.player then return end
    if self.started < 0 then
        -- clips load asynchronously: the timeline starts with the clip
        if self.player:isLoaded() then
            self.player:play(self.clip)
            self.started = T.frame
        end
        return
    end
    local n = T.frame - self.started
    if n % 15 == 0 and n <= 240 then
        local state = self.player:getState(self.clip)
        T.logAt("beacon", n, "clip", state.time, state.normalizedTime, self.player:isPlaying(self.clip),
                self.go.position, self.pulses)
    end
end

function Beacon:onBeaconPulse(strength, label)
    self.pulses = self.pulses + 1
    T.state.pulses = T.state.pulses + 1
    T.logAt("beacon", T.frame - self.started, "pulse", self.pulses, strength, label)
end

return Beacon

-- The main camera follows the Player from an offset, smoothly.
---@class CameraFollow : ScriptInstance
local CameraFollow = {
    properties = {
        { name = "target", displayName = "Target", type = "GameObject" },
        { name = "offset", displayName = "Offset", type = "vector3", default = { 0, 6, 11 } },
        { name = "smoothing", displayName = "Smoothing", type = "float", default = 4.0 },
    }
}

function CameraFollow:init()
    self.camera = Camera(self.scene, self.entity)
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function CameraFollow:onUpdate()
    if not self.target then return end
    local t = self.target:getWorldPosition()
    local p = self.camera.position
    local k = math.min(1, Engine.deltatime * self.smoothing)
    local goal = Vector3(t.x + self.offset.x, t.y + self.offset.y, t.z + self.offset.z)
    self.camera.position = p + (goal - p) * k
    self.camera:setTarget(t.x, t.y, t.z)
end

return CameraFollow

arguments.name: Gem
arguments.content:
-- A gem: spins, and is collected when the Player comes close.
---@class Gem : ScriptInstance
local Gem = {
    properties = {
        { name = "value", displayName = "Value", type = "int", default = 1 },
        { name = "spinSpeed", displayName = "Spin Speed", type = "float", default = 90.0 },
        { name = "radius", displayName = "Pickup Radius", type = "float", default = 1.1 },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Gem:init()
    self.go = GameObject(self.scene, self.entity)
    local player = self.scene:findEntity("Player")
    -- the courier's body: its Transform is interpolated for drawing (see Level.lua)
    self.player = player ~= 0 and Rigidbody(self.scene, player) or nil
    self.angle = 0
    self.collected = false
    T.state.gems = (T.state.gems or 0) + 1
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function Gem:onUpdate()
    if self.collected then return end
    self.angle = (self.angle + self.spinSpeed * Engine.deltatime) % 360
    self.go:setRotation(0, self.angle, 0)
    if self.player then
        local p = self.player.position
        local g = self.go:getWorldPosition()
        local dx, dz = p.x - g.x, p.z - g.z
        if dx * dx + dz * dz < self.radius * self.radius and math.abs(p.y - g.y) < 2.0 then
            self:collect()
        end
    end
end

function Gem:collect()
    self.collected = true
    T.state.score = T.state.score + self.value
    T.state.pickups = T.state.pickups + 1
    T.log("pickup", self.go.name, self.value, T.state.score)
    -- the Director plays the pickup sound and the burst where the gem was
    T.state.pending = T.state.pending or {}
    table.insert(T.state.pending, self.go:getWorldPosition())
    self.go:setActive(false)
end

return Gem

-- The HTML HUD of Level 1: the score and the gems collected.
---@class HudUI : ScriptInstance
local HudUI = { properties = {} }

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function HudUI:init()
    self.doc = UIDocument(self.scene, self.entity)
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function HudUI:onUpdate()
    local score = self.doc:getElementById("score")
    local gems = self.doc:getElementById("gems")
    if score then score.textContent = tostring(T.state.score) end
    if gems then
        gems.textContent = "gems " .. T.state.pickups .. "/" .. (T.state.gems or 0)
        if T.state.gems and T.state.pickups >= T.state.gems then gems.classList:add("all") end
    end
end

return HudUI

-- The HUD child scene (the engine's own UI components): a score Text, a time Progressbar.
---@class LegacyHud : ScriptInstance
local LegacyHud = {
    properties = {
        { name = "label", displayName = "Score Label", type = "Text" },
        { name = "timeBar", displayName = "Time Bar", type = "Progressbar" },
        { name = "duration", displayName = "Duration (frames)", type = "int", default = 360 },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function LegacyHud:init()
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function LegacyHud:onUpdate()
    -- first what the previous frame showed (its score was final), then this frame's values
    if T.scene == "Level1" and T.frame % 30 == 0 and self.label and self.timeBar then
        T.log("legacy_hud", self.label.text, self.timeBar.value)
    end
    if self.label then self.label.text = "Score " .. T.state.score end
    if self.timeBar then self.timeBar.value = math.min(1, T.frame / self.duration) end
end

return LegacyHud

arguments.name: Level
arguments.content:
-- Level 1 director: counts the frames, plays the pickup feedback, prints the transcript and
-- moves on to the next scene.
---@class Level : ScriptInstance
local Level = {
    properties = {
        { name = "duration", displayName = "Duration (frames)", type = "int", default = 360 },
        { name = "nextScene", displayName = "Next Scene", type = "string", default = "Arena2D" },
        { name = "pickupSound", displayName = "Pickup Sound", type = "AudioSource" },
        { name = "burst", displayName = "Pickup Burst", type = "ParticleSystem" },
        { name = "hud", displayName = "HUD", type = "UIDocument" },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Level:init()
    T.enter("Level1")
    T.schedule("Level1", {
        { Input.KEY_RIGHT, 20, 80 }, { Input.KEY_UP, 80, 130 }, { Input.KEY_SPACE, 140, 142 },
        { Input.KEY_LEFT, 150, 210 }, { Input.KEY_DOWN, 210, 250 }, { Input.KEY_SPACE, 260, 262 },
    })
    self.player = GameObject(self.scene, self.scene:findEntity("Player"))
    self.body = Rigidbody(self.scene, self.player.entity)
    -- physics state is read from the bodies: a GameObject's Transform is drawn between the last
    -- two fixed steps (physics interpolation), as far as the frame's leftover time, which a
    -- loading frame changes
    self.crates = {}
    for i = 1, 3 do
        local e = self.scene:findEntity("Crate " .. i)
        if e ~= 0 then self.crates[#self.crates + 1] = { name = "Crate " .. i, body = Rigidbody(self.scene, e) } end
    end
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onPostUpdate")
    T.log("setup", #self.crates, T.state.gems or 0, self.pickupSound ~= nil, self.burst ~= nil, self.hud ~= nil)
end

function Level:onUpdate()
    local pending = T.state.pending
    if pending and #pending > 0 then
        for _, position in ipairs(pending) do
            if self.pickupSound then
                self.pickupSound:stop()
                self.pickupSound:play()
                T.state.sfx = T.state.sfx + 1
            end
            if self.burst then
                local fx = GameObject(self.scene, self.burst.target)
                fx.position = position
                self.burst:start()
                T.state.bursts = T.state.bursts + 1
            end
        end
        T.state.pending = {}
    end
end

function Level:onPostUpdate()
    local f = T.frame
    if f % 10 == 0 then
        T.log("player", self.body.position, self.body.linearVelocity, T.state.score, T.state.pickups)
    end
    if f % 30 == 0 then
        for _, crate in ipairs(self.crates) do
            T.log("crate", crate.name, crate.body.position, crate.body.rotation)
        end
        if self.hud then
            local score = self.hud:getElementById("score")
            local gems = self.hud:getElementById("gems")
            T.log("hud", score and score.textContent or "?", gems and gems.textContent or "?",
                  gems ~= nil and gems.classList:contains("all"))
        end
        T.log("fx", T.state.sfx, T.state.bursts, self.burst ~= nil and self.burst:isRunning())
    end
    if f == self.duration then
        T.log("summary", T.state.score, T.state.pickups, T.state.pulses)
        SceneManager.loadScene(self.nextScene)
    end
    T.step()
end

return Level

-- The courier: a dynamic Rigidbody pushed by the arrow keys, Space jumps.
---@class Player : ScriptInstance
local Player = {
    properties = {
        { name = "acceleration", displayName = "Acceleration", type = "float", default = 14.0 },
        { name = "jumpSpeed", displayName = "Jump Speed", type = "float", default = 5.5 },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Player:init()
    self.go = GameObject(self.scene, self.entity)
    self.body = Rigidbody(self.scene, self.entity)
    self.jumps = 0
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onFixedUpdate")
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function Player:onFixedUpdate()
    local fx, fz = 0, 0
    if T.held(Input.KEY_RIGHT) then fx = fx + 1 end
    if T.held(Input.KEY_LEFT) then fx = fx - 1 end
    if T.held(Input.KEY_UP) then fz = fz - 1 end
    if T.held(Input.KEY_DOWN) then fz = fz + 1 end
    if fx ~= 0 or fz ~= 0 then
        -- a force of mass x acceleration: the body's mass comes from its collider and density
        local f = self.body.mass * self.acceleration
        self.body:applyForce(Vector3(fx * f, 0, fz * f))
    end
end

function Player:onUpdate()
    if T.pressed(Input.KEY_SPACE) then
        local v = self.body.linearVelocity
        self.body.linearVelocity = Vector3(v.x, self.jumpSpeed, v.z)
        self.jumps = self.jumps + 1
        T.log("jump", self.jumps)
    end
end

return Player

-- The robot waves with a Pose Animation on its Pose Animator.
---@class Robot : ScriptInstance
local Robot = {
    properties = {
        { name = "speed", displayName = "Speed", type = "float", default = 1.0 },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Robot:init()
    self.anim = Model(self.scene, self.entity):getPoseAnimator()
    self.started = -1
    self.finished = 0
    self.anim.onFinish = function() self.finished = self.finished + 1 end
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
end

function Robot:onUpdate()
    if self.started < 0 then
        -- the model loads asynchronously: the timeline starts with the animation
        if self.anim:isLoaded() then
            self.anim:setSpeed(self.speed)
            self.anim:play()
            self.started = T.frame
            T.logAt("robot", 0, "poses", self.anim:getPoseCount(), self.anim:getPoseName(0), self.anim:getLength())
        end
        return
    end
    local n = T.frame - self.started
    if n % 20 == 0 and n <= 240 then
        T.logAt("robot", n, "pose", self.anim:getTime(), self.anim:isPlaying(), self.finished)
    end
end

return Robot

-- Title screen: an HTML UI menu. Enter (or a click on Play) starts the game.
---@class Title : ScriptInstance
local Title = {
    properties = {
        { name = "nextScene", displayName = "Next Scene", type = "string", default = "Level1" },
        { name = "startDelay", displayName = "Start Delay (frames)", type = "int", default = 6 },
    }
}

local T = require("lib.transcript")

function Title:init()
    T.enter("Title")
    T.schedule("Title", { { Input.KEY_ENTER, 30, 32 } })
    self.doc = UIDocument(self.scene, self.entity)
    self.startAt = -1
    self.clicks = 0
    self.onPlay = function(event)
        self.clicks = self.clicks + 1
        self:begin("click")
    end
    RegisterEvent(self, self.doc.onLoad, "bind")
    self:bind()
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onUpdate")
    RegisterEngineEvent(self, "onPostUpdate")
end

function Title:bind()
    local play = self.doc:getElementById("play")
    if play then play:addEventListener("click", self.onPlay) end
end

function Title:begin(how)
    if self.startAt >= 0 then return end
    self.startAt = T.frame + self.startDelay
    local status = self.doc:getElementById("status")
    if status then
        status.textContent = "Starting (" .. how .. ")"
        status.classList:add("ready")
    end
    T.log("start", how)
end

function Title:onUpdate()
    if T.pressed(Input.KEY_ENTER) then self:begin("enter") end
    local ticks = self.doc:getElementById("ticks")
    if ticks then ticks.textContent = "frame " .. T.frame end
    if self.startAt >= 0 and T.frame == self.startAt then
        T.log("load", self.nextScene)
        SceneManager.loadScene(self.nextScene)
    end
end

function Title:onPostUpdate()
    if T.frame % 10 == 0 then
        local ticks = self.doc:getElementById("ticks")
        local status = self.doc:getElementById("status")
        T.log("ui", ticks and ticks.textContent or "?", status and status.textContent or "?",
              status ~= nil and status.classList:contains("ready"), self.clicks)
    end
    T.step()
end

return Title

-- Behaviour transcript of the upgrade fixture (tools/ci/upgrade_from_main).
-- Every scene's Director counts the scene's frames and prints the gameplay state as lines
--   T|<scene>|<frame>|<key>|<value>|...
-- that an old and a new editor (or player) must print identically. Shared by every script of
-- the game through require: one table for the whole play session.
local T = {
    scene = "",
    frame = 0,        -- frames since the scene's Director started (its onPostUpdate counts them)
    total = 0,        -- frames since the game started
    done = false,     -- the last scene ended its run
    state = { score = 0, pickups = 0, sfx = 0, bursts = 0, pulses = 0, contacts = 0 },
}

-- Autopilot: the game plays its own input schedule (exported players, the web), instead of
-- the keys an agent sends through the editor's send_input.
T.autopilot = (os.getenv ~= nil and os.getenv("UPGRADE_AUTOPILOT") == "1") or Engine.platform == Platform.Web
-- The autopilot also fixes the clock: every frame advances exactly 1/60 s whatever the machine's
-- speed (the editor runs do the same through the play tool's fixed_fps)
if T.autopilot then
    Engine.fixedDeltatime = 1 / 60
end
-- Exported desktop players quit after the last scene when asked to
T.exitAtEnd = os.getenv ~= nil and os.getenv("UPGRADE_EXIT_AT_END") == "1"

local function num(v)
    local s = string.format("%.3f", v)
    if s == "-0.000" then s = "0.000" end
    return s
end

function T.fmt(v)
    local t = type(v)
    if t == "number" then
        if math.type(v) == "integer" then return tostring(v) end
        return num(v)
    elseif t == "boolean" then
        return v and "true" or "false"
    elseif t == "nil" then
        return "nil"
    elseif t == "string" then
        return v
    end
    -- Vector2 / Vector3 / Vector4 / Quaternion userdata
    local ok, x = pcall(function() return v.x end)
    if ok and x ~= nil then
        local parts = { num(v.x), num(v.y) }
        local okz, z = pcall(function() return v.z end)
        if okz and z ~= nil then parts[#parts + 1] = num(z) end
        local okw, w = pcall(function() return v.w end)
        if okw and w ~= nil then parts[#parts + 1] = num(w) end
        return "(" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. ")"
    end
    return tostring(v)
end

function T.log(key, ...)
    if T.done then return end   -- after the end line: a player left running (the web) adds nothing
    local parts = { "T", T.scene, tostring(T.frame), key }
    for i = 1, select("#", ...) do
        parts[#parts + 1] = T.fmt((select(i, ...)))
    end
    print(table.concat(parts, "|"))
end

-- A line on a timeline of its own: frames counted from when something started (a clip, a
-- model that loads asynchronously), so the scene frame it started on stays out of the line
function T.logAt(timeline, frame, key, ...)
    if T.done then return end
    local parts = { "T", T.scene, timeline .. "+" .. tostring(frame), key }
    for i = 1, select("#", ...) do
        parts[#parts + 1] = T.fmt((select(i, ...)))
    end
    print(table.concat(parts, "|"))
end

function T.enter(scene)
    T.scene = scene
    T.frame = 0
    T.log("enter", T.autopilot)
end

-- Called once per frame by the scene's Director, from onPostUpdate (after every onUpdate)
function T.step()
    T.frame = T.frame + 1
    T.total = T.total + 1
end

function T.finish()
    T.log("end", T.total, T.state.score)
    T.done = true
    if T.exitAtEnd then
        io.stdout:flush()
        os.exit(0)
    end
end

-- Input: the real keys, or the autopilot's schedule of the scene ({key, from, to} frames)
-- (public: the editor-driven runs read it to send the same keys through send_input)
T.schedules = {}
function T.schedule(scene, list)
    T.schedules[scene] = list
end

function T.held(key)
    if not T.autopilot then
        return Input.isKeyPressed(key)
    end
    for _, s in ipairs(T.schedules[T.scene] or {}) do
        if s[1] == key and T.frame >= s[2] and T.frame < s[3] then return true end
    end
    return false
end

-- True on the first frame a key is held (scripts keep no per-key state)
local previous = {}
function T.pressed(key)
    local now = T.held(key)
    local id = T.scene .. ":" .. tostring(key)
    local was = previous[id]
    previous[id] = now
    return now and not was
end

return T
